questions_and_answers.question: When you are involved in a car accident, what should you do first?

answers.answer: Call your office in the U.S.

questions_and_answers.question: How do you say that there has been a car accident?

answers.answer: Kuruma no jiko desu. (There has been a car accident.)

questions_and_answers.question: How do you say that there are injured persons?

answers.answer: Keganin ga imasu. (There are injured persons.)

questions_and_answers.question: How do you ask someone to call an ambulance, the police, or a doctor?
What is a good idea to always carry with you in case of an emergency?

answers.answer: A card with the phone numbers of the U.S. Embassy and other places you might wish to call

questions_and_answers.question: How do you ask someone to telephone a number you have written down? ('Please telephone this place.')
What particle is used after the name of the place you want to contact (when making a phone call)?
How do you say 'I want to make a call'?
What numbers do you dial to call the police and the fire department/ambulance in Japan?
Why will it be far easier to handle the situation if you can find a Japanese person to help you?

answers.answer: Because the police or fire department will ask you about the details of the accident
Because foreigners are not allowed to call 110 or 119
Because the embassy will not answer

questions_and_answers.question: When you need to talk with the police, what should you show them first?

answers.answer: Your meeshi (calling card), which gives them much of the information they need

articles.text:
1. What to do when you are involved in a car accident

When you are involved in a car accident, ask anyone around for help. When you want to say that there has been a car accident, you can say the following:

Kuruma no jiko desu.    There has been (literally, 'it is') a car accident.

If there are any injured persons, say:

Keganin ga imasu.    There are injured persons.

If you want to ask someone to call an ambulance, the police, and/or a doctor, you can use the following words and expressions:

kyuukyuusha    ambulance
keesatsu       police
isha           doctor

Kyuukyuusha/keesatsu/isha o yonde kudasai.    Please call an ambulance/the police/a doctor.

It is a good idea always to carry with you a card with the telephone numbers of the U.S. Embassy and other places you might wish to call in an emergency. Your meeshi can also be quite useful. If you wish to have someone make a call to a number you have written down, you can say:

Koko ni denwa shite kudasai.    Please telephone this place.

Denwa means 'telephone' and the phrase denwa site (kudasai) means 'please phone.' The particle ni is used after the name of the place you want to contact. When you want to make a phone call, you can say:

Denwa shitain desu.    I want to make a call.

Likewise, if you want to call the American Embassy, you can say:

Amerika Taishikan ni denwa shitain desu.

You should contact your office immediately if you are involved in an accident so that they can send help or give you suggestions as to what to do.

When you need to talk with the police, show them your meeshi first. It will give them much of the information they need.

When you call the police or an ambulance yourself, dial the following numbers:

police            110
fire/ambulance    119

However, since the police or fire department will ask you about the details of the accident, it will be far easier to handle the situation if you can find a Japanese person to help you.
